photo.description: A pound coin floating in mercury due to surface tension, see Gerridae#Ability_to_move_on_water's_surface.

photo.caption: Native mercury with cinnabar, Socrates mine, Sonoma County, California. Cinnabar sometimes alters to native mercury in the oxidized zone of mercury deposits.
photo.description: Mercury Locality: Socrates Mine, Sonoma County, California, USA (Locality at mindat.org) An extremely rich ore specimen liberally covered with shiny bubbles or drops of native mercury (quicksilver) and tiny streaks of cinnabar. Mercury is the only recognised mineral that is found as a liquid at room temperature. Cinnabar alters to native mercury in the oxidized zone of deposits. Native mercury is also quite rare. photo.caption: Water cooled mercury condenser used in gold mining to recover and recycle the mercury
photo.description: A water cooled mercury condenser attached to a retort furnace, originally used in gold mining at the Empire Mine in Grass Valley, California. The furnace was used to separate amalgam into gold and mercury. The mercury was then recycled. Photo by Jim Heaphy.

photo.caption: Mercury flasks used in gold mines
photo.description: Mercury flasks used in California gold mines, on display at the North Star Mine Powerhouse and Pelton Wheel Museum near Grass Valley, California. Photo by Jim Heaphy.

rights.fileTitle: File:Mercury in Ice Core Upper Fremont Glacier.svg

photo.fileTitle: File:Mercury in Ice Core Upper Fremont Glacier.svg
photo.caption: Amount of atmospheric mercury deposited at Wyoming's Upper Fremont Glacier over the last 270 years
photo.description: Atmospheric mercury deposition corresponds to volcanic and anthropogenic events over the past 270 years. Preindustrial deposition rates can be conservatively extrapolated to present time (4 ng/L; in green) to illustrate the increase during the past 100 years (in red) and significant decreases in the past 15-20 years.
